Q1: The failing assertion is in `tests/test_closed_reader_does_not_rerun_a_successful_command` in `tests/test_gh_retry_stdout_isolation.py` (line 242). It is already on `main` and runs the `gh_retry` success-path replay `cat "${stdout_file}" || _gh_retry_replay_rc=$?` in `scripts/gh_helpers.sh:1229`, which PR #9279 does not touch. Its own diagnostic docstring (lines 249-250) says ubuntu-26.04 runners replay through Rust coreutils and see rc=0. So #9279 is not at fault. GITHUB FACTS show PR #9246 is open, not merged, and titled "Fix the last two CI failures on ubuntu-26.04 runners (heartbeat clock, closed-reader test)", so it already delivers this work. A second fix to the same `gh_retry` lines from `main` (option A), or one on #9279's branch (option C), would compete with #9246 and conflict with it and with #9264 and #9316 (§9: extend existing mechanisms, never compete). Under the pipeline-capability rule we choose B without its manual tail. This issue makes no code change and waits on the blocked path until #9246 merges. The "close as duplicate" and "re-run #9279's CI" parts of B are not pipeline actions and are dropped.
Q2: This applies only if the hold on Q1 ends because #9246 closes without merging. In that case the fix goes in production, in `gh_retry`'s success-path replay at `scripts/gh_helpers.sh:1229`. The replay must detect the closed pipe (EPIPE or SIGPIPE) without depending on how the host's `cat` exits. Inline `gh_retry()` copies in `review_autofix.yml` (checked by `_inline_gh_retry` in the same test file) must be kept in step with it. The assertion at test line 242 must not be weakened. Options B and C would leave production returning 0 when a reader closes early, which breaks the contract the test protects.
